title.name: Pax Avant
title.subtitle: Shepherds of Roncal and Barétous
title.players: 1 or 2 players: most cheese wins… if the peace holds
menu.easy.note: Wolves give up sooner and the computer cheats less.
menu.normal.note: The real mountain: just enough grass, stubborn wolves and a neighbour with few scruples.
menu.solo.note: You are Roncal. The computer is Barétous, and it knows how to cheat too.
menu.duo.note: Player 1: Roncal. Player 2: Barétous. Most cheese wins, but if the peace breaks, you both score 0.
intro.1: Every summer, shepherds from Roncal (Navarre) and Barétous (Béarn, in France) take their flocks up to the pastures on the border.
intro.2: The mountain could not feed everyone. The quarrels over grass and springs were so bitter that people from both valleys died.
intro.3: In 1375 they made peace: turns to use the pass and its springs, and every year Barétous hands three cows to Roncal at the San Martín stone.
outro.1: The ceremony still takes place every 13 July, and the mayors still say "Pax avant": peace from now on.
outro.2: You can go and see it at the San Martín stone, high above the Belagua valley. Good neighbours share!
brief.title: A summer on the border
brief.goal: The valley that makes the most cheese wins: well-fed sheep give milk. You can cheat, but every trick uses up the peace. If it reaches 0, it's war and you both score 0.
brief.cpu: Barétous (square mark): played by the computer
brief.a: [A] whistle the dog: it pushes sheep (the neighbours' too)
brief.b: [B] ring the bell: your flock comes, wolves and bears back off
brief.c: [C] pick up a sheep (any sheep) or put it down
ceremony.0: 13 July. There was war this summer: nobody climbs to the stone. That's how summers ended before 1375.
ceremony.1: 13 July. There were tricks and shouting, but the peace held. The mayor of Isaba asks three times, "Do you want peace?": "Pax avant".
ceremony.2: 13 July. A party on the pass! Both valleys celebrate a good summer together.
ceremony.3: 13 July. The best party in years! Music, dancing and very good neighbours.
ceremony.cows: As the treaty says, Barétous hands three healthy cows to Roncal.

admin.title: Settings
fact.treaty: Roncal and Barétous made an agreement to share pastures and water. It is usually dated 1375, and it is still kept.
fact.arbiters: It is said the agreement was settled by arbiters from the Ansó valley in Aragón, after years of quarrels over pasture.
fact.stone: The San Martín stone stands on a mountain pass, right on the border between Spain and France.
fact.gesture: At the ceremony, the mayors lay their hands one on another on the stone and say "Pax avant": peace from now on.
fact.cows: Every year Barétous hands three cows to Roncal, as the agreement says. That is why it is called the Tribute of the Three Cows.
fact.oldest: It is often said to be one of the oldest treaties in Europe that is still in force.
fact.transhumance: In winter, Roncal shepherds walked their flocks south to the Bardenas Reales. Moving flocks with the seasons is called transhumance.
fact.cheese: Roncal cheese is made from sheep’s milk. It is said to be the first Spanish cheese with a protected designation of origin.
fact.mayors: The Roncal mayors come to the ceremony in their traditional dress: dark and solemn, with a cloak.
fact.today: The ceremony takes place every 13 July at the San Martín stone, above the Belagua valley. Anyone can go and watch.
fact.commons: A pasture eaten down to the earth takes a long time to recover. Sharing and resting pastures keeps the mountain healthy.
exit.title: Exit to the game menu?
fact.turns: In 1375 turns were set: Barétous used Navarre’s pastures for 28 days from 10 July, and Roncal from August.
fact.question: At the ceremony the mayor of Isaba asks three times, "Do you want peace?", and the French answer yes.
fact.justice: At the end, the mayor of Isaba judges last year’s breaches of the treaty. The border guards swear with a hand on his staff.
fact.quarrels: Before the treaty there were fights over the springs in which people from both valleys died. The peace of 1375 ended that.
fact.selection: A vet inspects the cows brought from France and chooses three for Roncal.
title.players@phone: 1 player: you are Roncal, the computer is Barétous

banner.title: Summer begins!
banner.text: Lead your flock to good grass. Cheese decides who wins.
banner.peace: Stealing sheep or grazing the neighbours' land uses up the peace. At 0: war.
tip.cheese: Well-fed sheep give milk: cheese for your valley.
tip.bell: Hold [B]: your flock follows you. Lead it to green grass.
tip.steal: [C] picks up a sheep. Put the neighbours' one down in your pen and it's yours… but it costs the peace.
tip.peace: The grass in the middle belongs to both. The neighbours' grass (with their flag) costs peace with every bite.
tip.dog: [A] sends the dog to push sheep. It can drive the neighbours' sheep into your pen.
tip.help: Scare a wolf off the neighbours' flock and the peace mends.
tip.last: Summer's nearly over! Keep your sheep well fed.
msg.wolf: A wolf is after the {valley} flock! Scare it off with the dog or the bell.
msg.wolves: A pack of wolves is after the {valley} flock!
msg.wolfLeaves: The wolf gets bored and leaves
msg.helpedText: {valley} helped the neighbours: the peace mends.
msg.bearText: One bell only shoves it (towards the neighbours?). Both bells at once drive it off the mountain.
msg.bearLeaves: The bear goes back to the forest
msg.tenseText: The peace is shaking. Help the neighbours or stop cheating.
msg.brinkText: One more trick and war breaks out: you'd both score 0.
msg.calm: The valleys are getting along again.
